The shortest war in history is the Anglo-Zanzibar War, fought on August 27, 1896 between the British Empire and the Sultanate of Zanzibar [d1][d3][d4][d9]. It lasted approximately 38 to 40 minutes (with some sources citing up to 43 minutes), beginning when British warships opened fire on the sultan's palace at 9:00 AM and ending when the white flag of surrender was raised [d5][d3][d4]. The war was triggered by the death of the pro-British Sultan Hamad bin Thuwaini and the refusal of Prince Khālid ibn Barghash to vacate the palace after a British ultimatum [d1][d4][d9]. The British Royal Navy emerged victorious, with over 500 Zanzibari casualties compared to just one British marine injured [d5][d3].
